title: Tuesday, 9:40 p.m.
intro: Pell Dentistry after hours. The sterilizer ticks. The lake is black in the window.

items.label: Records cabinet
items.text: Bottom drawer, behind the Pell family charts: a ledger bound in oilcloth. The last entry is dated 9 September 1961. 'A. Marsh, 9. Extraction, lower left. Paid in eggs.'

items.label: Desk drawer
items.text: A note in the Mayor's handwriting: 'Come at one. Bring the records.' The ink is fresh.

items.label: The dental chair
items.text: You sit in it. Facing the lake, the way every patient does. It is the calmest you have felt all day.

items.label: The window
items.text: The glass is very slightly rippling, as if it were water. Out on the lake a light flashes once, and stops. You wave without thinking. Something waves back.

items.label: Mags's diary
items.text: One line on the last page, underlined twice: 'Teeth don't lie.'

items.label: Sterilizer
items.text: It beeps, with great confidence, about nothing.

items.label: Bowl of mints
items.text: For the brave. You take two. You are not sure which category you are in.

items.label: X-ray light box
items.text: Silas's X-ray, still clipped up. Three tiny stamps glow back at you: CP. CP. CP.

items.label: Taped under the chair
items.text: A yellowed note, taped under the seat, in an old man's hand. It was left for whoever sat here next and cared enough to look.
